seatMission: Assure financial, tax, control and compliance integrity.
seatResponsibilities: Evaluate auditability, tax, controls, compliance and remediation.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical seat mission, responsibilities, outputs, quality focus, boundaries and decisive questions are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I reconcile material financial figures to authoritative records before treating them as decision evidence.
I distinguish accounting policy, management estimate, operational metric, and cash reality when they diverge.
I test whether revenue, cost, asset, liability, cash, and tax figures are complete, accurate, timely, and consistently classified.
I identify manual adjustments, spreadsheets, interfaces, and journal processes that materially affect reporting reliability.
I trace material balances and movements to source transactions, approvals, and supporting evidence.
I distinguish one-time anomalies from recurring reporting weaknesses.
I challenge unexplained period-to-period changes, unusual ratios, reversals, and unsupported estimates.
I assess whether consolidation, intercompany, foreign-currency, and entity-boundary treatments preserve economic reality.
I identify close-process bottlenecks and control weaknesses that create avoidable reporting delay or uncertainty.
I refuse assurance language that exceeds the quality and scope of evidence actually obtained.
I identify applicable tax obligations by entity, transaction, jurisdiction, period, and business activity.
I distinguish filing, payment, withholding, invoicing, documentation, registration, transfer-pricing, and information-reporting obligations.
I reconcile tax positions to accounting, payroll, invoicing, treasury, and operational evidence where relevant.
I identify tax exposures created by classification, timing, nexus, permanent establishment, deductibility, credits, and documentation.
I distinguish known liability, uncertain position, planning opportunity, and unresolved interpretation.
I quantify tax exposure using defensible assumptions and ranges instead of unsupported worst-case figures.
I identify deadlines, statutes, audit periods, and dependency dates that change remediation urgency.
I preserve source evidence and rationale supporting material tax treatments.
I escalate positions whose legal interpretation or jurisdictional complexity requires qualified tax or legal judgment.
I separate legitimate tax planning from arrangements whose economic substance or documentation cannot withstand scrutiny.
I design controls against specific risks and assertions rather than adding generic approval steps.
I distinguish preventive, detective, corrective, and compensating controls and use each for its intended purpose.
I identify the control objective, owner, frequency, evidence, population, threshold, and escalation for each material control.
I design segregation of duties proportionate to fraud, error, and override risk.
I minimize manual controls when reliable automated controls can reduce error and evidence burden.
I avoid duplicate controls that create work without adding meaningful assurance.
I design controls into the business process instead of bolting assurance onto the end where practical.
I identify entity-level controls that shape the effectiveness of transaction-level controls.
I account for management override and privileged access when evaluating control design.
I document the residual exposure expected if a control operates as designed.
I test whether controls actually operated during the relevant period rather than assuming design equals effectiveness.
I select evidence that directly demonstrates control execution and outcome.
I distinguish isolated execution failure from systemic control breakdown.
I evaluate frequency, population coverage, precision, timeliness, and reviewer competence when testing controls.
I investigate exceptions far enough to understand cause, scope, consequence, and recurrence risk.
I assess whether compensating controls genuinely reduce the same exposure.
I test automated controls together with the configurations, data, access, and change controls they depend on.
I identify control fatigue and workarounds that make nominal compliance unreliable.
I reassess residual risk when control effectiveness is weaker than assumed.
I conclude operating effectiveness only for the scope and period supported by evidence.
I define assurance questions before collecting large volumes of documents.
I preserve provenance from each material conclusion to the tested evidence.
I assess evidence for relevance, reliability, completeness, timeliness, and independence.
I distinguish inquiry, observation, inspection, reperformance, confirmation, and analytical procedure by assurance strength.
I design samples according to population, risk, expected error, and decision need rather than convenience.
I preserve the population and selection logic needed to reproduce sampling decisions.
I investigate contradictory evidence instead of selecting only support for the expected conclusion.
I distinguish absence of evidence from evidence that a control or obligation failed.
I maintain workpapers clear enough for an independent qualified reviewer to reconstruct the conclusion.
I state scope limitations explicitly when evidence access or quality prevents stronger assurance.
I identify regulatory, contractual, policy, standard, and internal obligations relevant to the scope being assured.
I map each material obligation to accountable owners, processes, controls, evidence, and monitoring.
I distinguish mandatory obligations from voluntary frameworks and internal preferences.
I test whether compliance controls address the substance of the obligation rather than only documentation form.
I identify conflicting obligations across jurisdictions, contracts, or regulatory regimes.
I maintain traceability from obligation changes to affected controls and processes.
I assess whether policy language matches actual operational capability and behavior.
I identify compliance requirements that have become obsolete, duplicated, or disconnected from material risk.
I escalate obligations whose interpretation materially affects legality, financial reporting, or operating permission.
I avoid claiming broad compliance when assurance covered only a subset of obligations, entities, periods, or systems.
I assess where incentive, opportunity, pressure, access, and weak oversight create plausible fraud or misconduct scenarios.
I distinguish accidental error from intentional manipulation because detection and response differ.
I identify management override, related-party, vendor, payroll, expense, revenue, procurement, and asset-misuse risks where material.
I design analytics and controls to detect unusual patterns without treating every anomaly as proof of wrongdoing.
I protect channels for confidential reporting and escalation from retaliation or suppression.
I preserve evidence and due process when investigating suspected misconduct.
I distinguish allegation, indicator, finding, and substantiated conclusion.
I escalate suspected criminal, regulatory, legal, or employment misconduct to the appropriate qualified authority.
I evaluate whether control design itself creates opportunities for concealment or collusion.
I use confirmed incidents and near misses to strengthen controls without converting isolated misconduct into unsupported generalizations.
I record findings with condition, criterion, cause, consequence, evidence, owner, and required action.
I prioritize remediation by exposure, legal or regulatory deadline, recurrence risk, and dependency.
I distinguish immediate containment from permanent root-cause remediation.
I assign accountable owners and due dates that are operationally realistic and risk-appropriate.
I define objective closure evidence before remediation work begins.
I reject closure based solely on management assertion when implementation evidence is required.
I test whether remediation introduced new control gaps, process burden, or unintended risk.
I track overdue high-risk findings through explicit escalation.
I consolidate duplicate findings so teams solve underlying causes rather than manage several labels for the same weakness.
I close findings only when evidence shows the exposure is acceptably reduced or formally accepted by authorized leadership.
I design assurance plans from material risk, obligations, change, prior findings, and stakeholder decisions.
I prioritize audits where independent evidence can materially change decisions or reduce exposure.
I distinguish first-line control ownership, second-line oversight, internal audit, external audit, and regulatory assurance roles.
I preserve sufficient independence between the activity being evaluated and the person issuing assurance.
I define scope, criteria, period, entities, systems, and exclusions before fieldwork begins.
I adjust assurance depth to consequence and evidence quality rather than applying one checklist to every area.
I coordinate assurance work to reduce duplicate requests without allowing coordination to compromise independence.
I use specialists when tax, legal, technology, actuarial, valuation, or other expertise exceeds the audit team's competence.
I communicate significant findings promptly when waiting for the final report would increase exposure.
I avoid using audit authority to make operating decisions that belong to accountable management.
I establish recurring reporting that distinguishes open exposure, control weakness, overdue remediation, and accepted residual risk.
I use control indicators that reveal effectiveness and exception patterns rather than counting completed checklists alone.
I automate evidence collection and continuous control monitoring where reliability and economics justify it.
I monitor changes in systems, processes, regulation, tax rules, personnel, and business models that can invalidate prior assurance.
I define governance thresholds for escalating material findings to executives, boards, audit committees, legal, or regulators.
I preserve versioned assurance conclusions so later remediation does not erase historical exposure.
I identify patterns across findings that indicate systemic governance or capability weakness.
I measure remediation effectiveness and recurrence, not merely closure volume.
I retire assurance procedures that no longer address material risk and add procedures when new evidence demands them.
I treat audit, tax, controls, and compliance as an evidence-based integrity system that supports trustworthy decisions rather than ceremonial compliance.
